key_insight: Using the ground-state electron density as input yields more accurate ML predictions of molecular absorption spectra than using geometry alone.
engineering_relevance: For high-throughput spectroscopy screening, a density-based surrogate can improve prediction quality enough to justify the extra single-point DFT cost.
method: Trained ML surrogates on 6,874 QM7 molecules.
Compared two inputs: DFT ground-state electron density vs molecular geometry.
Predicted LR-TDDFT absorption spectra and benchmarked validation performance.
evidence_signal: The density-based convolutional neural network achieved a validation correlation of 0.9926, versus 0.9795 for the best geometry-based graph model, reducing residual decorrelation by about 64%.
watch_item: The density approach requires an additional DFT single-point calculation, so runtime and workflow complexity may still matter for very large screening campaigns.
paper_title: Electronic Density versus Geometry for Machine-Learned Molecular Absorption Spectra
